clue.text: Fellow fire raisers (first three) and fellows in 'all must now be gone less than 70 years

definitions.text: must now be gone less than 70 years
definitions.note: describes a work still protected: its author has been dead for under 70 years

indicators.note: only the opening three letters of the fire raisers are kept, the rest dropped

blocks.note: co- is the prefix for a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
pyromaniacs are people who start fires
college fellows dine at high table in hall; the dropped H of 'all says to drop the H of high too

explanation.surface: A grim little reckoning that all the arsonists and their college colleagues will be dead within seventy years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IGH TABLE is high table spoken Cockney-fashion, as 'all is hall. This 13-letter word is also the theme's key: written over the other 13 letters of the alphabet, it pairs letters to encipher the theme entries.
explanation.definitionFit: UK copyright runs for 70 years after the author's death, so a protected work is one whose author died less than 70 years ago.

clue.text: Missile piercing goddess, having been finally misdirected, was produced in Lebanon

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: the tree is what Lebanon grew, and it is on the national flag

indicators.note: piercing means pushed into, so the missile goes inside the goddess
the goddess's last letter, S for south, is turned to E for east

blocks.note: Ceres is the Roman goddess of the harvest
a dart is a thrown missile

explanation.surface: A goddess struck by a stray missile turns out to be something made in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the goddess's final S as the compass point south and redirect it to E, east; then the dart pierces the result after CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon is the country's emblem, so a cedar tree is the thing Lebanon famously grew.

clue.text: Play buried by 8 after 20's strike

blocks.note: first meaning: Shakespeare's Roman tragedy
second meaning: the man himself, whom 8, Antony, comes to bury after 20, Brutus, has struck him down

explanation.walkthrough: Antony says he comes to bury Caesar, not to praise him, after Brutus and the others have stabbed him. Like every theme entry the title is enciphered by the COPYRIGHTABLE key, so it is entered PTXNTH DVZHVM.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar is both the play and the man in it whom Antony buries after the stabbing.

clue.text: Conductor wants something on toast, being all mouth

definitions.note: a phrase for a noun: someone who is all mouth is an empty chatterer

blocks.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a British orchestral conductor
pâté is commonly spread on toast

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader asks for a snack on toast and talks without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlepate is an empty-headed, chattering person, all talk with nothing behind it.

clue.text: Complaint that 24 lacks love

indicators.note: lacks means is missing, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: 24's answer is LEAVE OUT, and leave means go, so it becomes go out
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A grumble that the answer to another clue is missing its love.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue leans on 24: LEAVE OUT is reworded as GO OUT, and dropping an O from that leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout is a painful inflammation of the joints, and complaint is the usual word for an ailment.

clue.text: Second speaker, perhaps

blocks.note: reads as a debater who speaks next, but means something that speaks every second
flags the definition as a playful example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the next person to rise in a debate; the answer is the sound a clock makes each second.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock says tick-tock with every passing second, so its sound is a speaker of seconds.

clue.text: The two first ministers of apartheid

definitions.note: plural because two prime ministers had this surname: Louis Botha and P W Botha

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: both means the two of them
its first letter, A

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the two men who first led apartheid-era governments.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Botha was the first prime minister of the Union of South Africa and P W Botha a later apartheid leader, so the surname covers two ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two South African prime ministers bore the surname Botha, so the single name stands for both ministers.

clue.text: Last saint for salad

blocks.note: the end is the last part
St Ives is named after a saint, Ive or Ia

explanation.surface: A final saint is offered in exchange for some salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a bitter leaf grown for salads, so a bowl of endives is salad.

clue.text: Girl slightly involved with toy boy

definitions.note: Antony is a boy's name, and Cleopatra's lover was hardly her toy boy

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the girl and the toy are mixed together

blocks.note: Ann is a girl's name
taken as written, its letters mixed in with the girl's

explanation.surface: A girl has a mild fling with a much younger man.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the hub of the theme, Mark Antony. Entered through the COPYRIGHTABLE cipher, each letter swapping with its partner, A-N-T-O-N-Y goes into the grid as VIUFIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony is a male first name, and the toy boy in the surface hints at Cleopatra's Roman lover.

clue.text: Finger put in book

blocks.note: first meaning: the forefinger, the finger you point with
second meaning: to list in a book's alphabetical guide at the back

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings of one word: a digit and a verb for listing something in a reference section.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the pointing digit, and to index a book is to compile its alphabetical list of topics.

clue.text: Short series on pet kept by small boy

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the small boy's name wraps round the rest

blocks.note: Ted is a short boy's name
a run is a series, as in a run of wins
a cat is a typical household pet

explanation.surface: A little boy keeps a pet and a short run of something, perhaps a comic serial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something truncated has been cut short, so the adjective means shortened.

clue.text: The ancient woodland of Paris in a crystal ball?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: what is seen in a crystal ball has been predicted

blocks.note: forêt is French for forest, the woodland a Parisian would name
old means ancient

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's crystal ball shows the old forest of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word is written before the English one, although the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Events glimpsed in a seer's crystal ball are prophesied ones, and the question mark admits that this is a playful definition.

clue.text: 8's wife mentioned in his play and by Tawney?

definitions.text: 8's wife mentioned in his play and by Tawney?

blocks.note: 8 is Antony, and his first wife is spoken of in Antony and Cleopatra but never appears on stage
the tawny one is Cleopatra, whose tawny front opens the play, and she talks about this wife often

explanation.walkthrough: Antony's wife Fulvia dies offstage, so she is only ever mentioned. As a theme entry she is entered in the COPYRIGHTABLE cipher: each letter swaps with its partner, so F-U-L-V-I-A goes in as OTXANV.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulvia, Mark Antony's first wife, is spoken of in Shakespeare's play but never seen, which is exactly what the clue says.

clue.text: Automatic pilot for top player

blocks.note: George is British airmen's slang for the autopilot
best means top, the finest

explanation.surface: An aircraft's autopilot is said to suit the finest performer.
explanation.walkthrough: George Best was the Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Best was one of the most celebrated footballers of the 1960s, a player of genius.

clue.text: Entry for the Booker brought by road

definitions.note: a kerb is the edge that runs beside the road

indicators.note: an entry for something goes into it, so the answer is found inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Booker and the start of brought

explanation.surface: A novel submitted for the Booker Prize arrives by van rather than by post.
explanation.walkthrough: The Booker is the literary prize, but here the word only donates its last three letters to the hidden answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb is the raised stone edging beside the roadway, so it lies by the road.

clue.text: You sound like (first to last) a tea girl

definitions.note: U sounds like you, and U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the first letter of the tea word goes round to its end

blocks.note: cupper is an informal spelling of cuppa, a cup of tea
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone is told they talk like the girl who serves the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Mitford's U and non-U sorted English usage by class, with U meaning upper class; so a letter that sounds like you stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Mitford's scheme U is the upper class, and U is pronounced exactly like the word you.

clue.text: Boat holder endlessly struggles with fish

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: an anchor holds a boat in place
vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: Something that holds a boat fights a losing battle with a catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchovies are small, strongly flavoured fish of the herring family.

clue.text: On its way about — not far off a week

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: something sent is on its way
nigh means near, not far off

explanation.surface: A parcel is on its way and will take nearly a week to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sennight is an archaic contraction of seven nights, meaning a week.

clue.text: Is it a police job to clean round most of the dining room?

definitions.note: a question asking whether the answer is a police post; French police are run from a préfecture

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the word for clean surrounds the room
most of a word means its tail is cut away

blocks.note: pure means clean
a refectory is the dining hall of a monastery or college

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether scrubbing the canteen counts as police work.
explanation.walkthrough: A refectory is the dining hall of a monastery or college; the question mark covers a definition by example, since a French préfecture is a police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: In France the Préfecture de police runs policing in Paris, so the prefect's office is a police appointment.

clue.text: Two-piece suit for party ends with immobilisation, as follows

indicators.note: the ends of the word are its first and last letters
follows means comes after, so as goes on the end

blocks.note: the first and last letters of party, P and Y
a jam is a state where nothing can move
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dress suit for a party ends up stuck, as described below.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas are a loose jacket and trousers for sleeping in, a two-piece suit for bed.

clue.text: Bargepole touches beast

indicators.note: touches means sits right up against, so the two pieces join end to end

blocks.note: the word splits: Barge is the definition, and its pole half is S, the south pole
a cow is a farm beast

explanation.surface: Someone pushing a barge along pokes an animal on the bank with the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first word splits in two: Barge is the definition and pole is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used as a lighter, a kind of barge.

clue.text: Transport without the groove?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the vehicle is wrapped round the groove

blocks.note: a bus is a means of transport
a rut is a groove worn in a road

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about vehicles that run without rails or grooves.
explanation.walkthrough: The man is not defined here; the theme does that, since 20 is the assassin whose strike and wife other clues mention. Brutus is enciphered with the COPYRIGHTABLE key and entered WMTUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus, Caesar's friend and assassin, is the 20 whose strike and whose wife Portia the other theme clues name.

clue.text: See 2
20's wife mentioned in 8's Italianate play

blocks.note: first meaning: 20 is Brutus, and his wife comes to him the night before the assassination in Julius Caesar
second meaning: the heroine of The Merchant of Venice, whose title merchant Antonio is 8's name in Italian

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare used the same name twice: for Brutus's wife, and for the Belmont heiress in the Venetian play where Antonio, the Italian form of Antony, is the merchant. As a theme entry it is enciphered by the COPYRIGHTABLE key and entered JFMUNV.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia is Brutus's wife in Julius Caesar and also the clever heiress who saves Antonio in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Park in Cold Comfort country must be destroyed

blocks.note: the rustics of Cold Comfort Farm say mun for must
to go is to be destroyed or done away with

explanation.surface: A rural park in Cold Comfort country is due for demolition.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold Comfort Farm is Stella Gibbons's comic novel set among Sussex farmers who speak in broad dialect. Mungo, shoddy cloth made from shredded rags, takes its name from the dialect phrase it mun go.
explanation.definitionFit: Mungo Park was the Scottish explorer of the Niger, so his first name answers to Park.

clue.text: Skip hire circulating — have you lost your heads?

definitions.note: to skip a passage is to leave it out

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the word for hire surrounds the rest
the two words lose their first letters, which leaves AVE and OU

blocks.note: to let a property is to hire it out
have with its head, the H, taken off
you with its head, the Y, taken off

explanation.surface: A man renting out skips asks two customers whether they have gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a large builder's waste container, hired by the week in Britain; here it is the verb meaning to miss out.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a page or a step is to omit it, which is the phrasal verb exactly.

clue.text: Leader of reconstruction in London

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
in means placed inside the next piece

blocks.note: Cobbett called London the Great Wen, a wen being a swelling
its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A history note on the man who led London's rebuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the man: Sir Christopher Wren led the rebuilding of London after the Great Fire of 1666, and the wordplay puts the first letter of reconstruction inside London's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's and dozens of City churches in the rebuilding after the Great Fire.

clue.text: Fellows on Silver Lake are animals

blocks.note: men are fellows
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Some men on Silver Lake turn out to be wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for show, so the word stands for animals as a group.

clue.text: Fellow is given time for crime

blocks.note: he stands for a male, a fellow
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A man is sentenced to a stretch for what he did.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing time suggests prison, but time is only its abbreviation, added to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a large and planned one, so it is a kind of crime.

clue.text: Paper found by stopwatch?

blocks.note: first meaning: a London racing newspaper, the Pink 'Un
second meaning, read literally: the times in sport that a stopwatch records

explanation.walkthrough: The name of the newspaper also describes, literally, what a stopwatch measures at a race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sporting Times was a Victorian London weekly about racing, and sporting times are also the times a stopwatch records.
